title: Commercial Code
text:
Law: Commercial Code
Reference: Law 33/2007
Date of Promulgation: Approved by the People’s Assembly on November 27, 2007

Promulgated by President Bashar Al-Assad on December 9, 2007

Relevant Provisions:
The Commercial Code consists of four books:

General Principles of Commerce, Merchants and Commercial Establishments- touches on the various commercial activities;

Commercial Contracts- correspond to the development of the financial sector in Syria in recent years including in such areas as mortgages and charges over assets, agencies and brokerages, and banking activities;

Negotiable Instruments- lays down rules for bills of exchange, promissory notes, cheques and bonds; and

Insolvency- sets down the procedures for individual and company voluntary arrangements, and bankruptcy proceedings.

Related Legislation:
Replaces the old Commercial Code found in Legislative Decree 149/1949.

Historical Context:
With the changes in economic policy towards a social market economy taking place, the new Commercial Code sought to promote the Syrian market as a potential base for local and foreign investors.
